record.context_brief: When lens spaces are spectrally unique
record.original_question: For which dimensions 2n − 1 and orders q of the fundamental group is every lens space of volume vol(S^(2n−1))/q spectrally unique within the class of lens spaces with that same dimension and group order, so that no nontrivial isospectrality occurs?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.7. Provide conditions on n and q such that L•(n, q) = L(n, q); that is, for which no (non-trivial) isospectrality is possible among (2n − 1)-dimensional lens spaces with volume vol(S2n−1)/q.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n\ge 2$ and an integer $q\ge 2$, a $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens space is a quotient $L(q;s_1,\dots,s_n) = S^{2n-1}/\Gamma$, where $S^{2n-1}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ is the unit sphere with its round metric and $\Gamma\cong\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ acts freely by 
$$(z_1,\dots,z_n)\mapsto (e^{2\pi i s_1/q}z_1,\dots, e^{2\pi i s_n/q}z_n),$$
with $\gcd(s_j,q)=1$ for all $j$. Each such lens space inherits a Riemannian metric of constant curvature $1$ and volume $\mathrm{vol}(S^{2n-1})/q$. Let $L(n,q)$ denote the set of isometry classes of such $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens spaces with fundamental group of order $q$, and let $L^\bullet(n,q)\subseteq L(n,q)$ denote the subset of isometry classes which are uniquely determined within $L(n,q)$ by the spectrum of the Laplace–Beltrami operator (i.e., no other element of $L(n,q)$ is isospectral but non-isometric to it).

Problem: Determine all pairs $(n,q)$ with $n\ge 2$, $q\ge 2$ for which $L^\bullet(n,q) = L(n,q)$, i.e., for which no nontrivial isospectrality occurs among $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens spaces of volume $\mathrm{vol}(S^{2n-1})/q$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: Ikeda–Yamamoto proved three-dimensional lens spaces and homogeneous lens spaces are determined by their Laplace spectrum within the class of lens spaces, and certain low-dimensional cases (including some orbifold versions in dimensions 3 and 4) are known. However, a full characterization of all pairs (n,q) for which no nontrivial isospectrality occurs among (2n−1)-dimensional lens spaces remains an open problem, with many isospectral non-isometric families known to exist in higher dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Isospectrality For Orbifold Lens Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Ikeda and Yamamoto proved that homogeneous lens spaces and three dimensional lens spaces are completely determined by the spectra of their Laplace-Beltrami operators in the class of all lens spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Spectral uniqueness within the class of lens spaces is known only in special cases (homogeneous and 3-dimensional).

status_evidence.title: Spectrally distinguishing symmetric spaces II
status_evidence.snippet: Isospectral non-isometric lens spaces exist in many dimensions, showing complete spectral determination fails generally.
status_evidence.claim: Nontrivial isospectrality among lens spaces occurs for many (n,q), so a full classification is not established.
